summary: This PositivePsychology.com article explains healthy (adaptive) coping mechanisms, drawing on research on coping, hope, positive emotions and resilience. It covers how to foster coping through positivity, lists six types of positive coping strategies (relaxation, coping statements, positive self-talk, community support, attitude and outlook, religious practices), and describes proactive coping, awe, and DBT's coping ahead skill. It closes with two real-life examples (Tabatha Doherty and John Bienvenu), worksheets, and resources from the site.
one_line: A PositivePsychology.com guide to adaptive coping strategies, including six positive coping types, proactive coping, awe, and real-life examples.
key_facts: Algorani and Gupta (2021, p. 1) describe coping as "thoughts and behaviors mobilized to manage internal and external stressful situations."
Adaptive coping strategies include active planning and positive reframing, while maladaptive strategies such as denial, venting, and substance abuse often result in undesirable consequences.
Folkman (2010, p. 901) posits that hope is not an "automatically self-renewing resource" and must be nurtured.
Snyder et al. (2005, p. 257) state that "hopeful thought reflects the belief that one can find pathways to desired goals and become motivated to use those pathways."
Fredrickson (2009, p. 61) says that people who enjoyed more positivity were more able to cope with adversity in an open-minded way and saw more solutions.
Fredrickson's list of daily practices that foster positivity includes being sincere, savoring goodness, counting your blessings, and connecting with nature.
Gloria and Steinhardt (2016, p. 146) found evidence that individual resilience can moderate the impact of stress on anxiety and depressive symptoms.
Bourne (2015, p. 88) defines deep relaxation as a "distinct psychological state that is the exact opposite of the way your body reacts under stress."
Bourne (2015) lists relaxation ideas including abdominal breathing, progressive muscle relaxation, visualization, yoga, grounding, and physical exercise.
Bourne (2015, p. 195) describes positive self-talk as "writing down and rehearsing positive statements that directly refute or invalidate your negative self-talk."

Frydenberg (2020, p. 88) describes proactive coping as the "appraisal of demands as challenges" and consists of active coping, self-efficacy, anticipatory behavior, and planning and utilizing social resources.
Sun et al. (2023) state that awe can be cultivated through natural wonders and landscapes, paranormal phenomena, art, and artifacts.
Coping ahead is a skill within Dialectical Behavior Therapy, as described by Linehan (2015), that helps clients expect and plan for emotional circumstances associated with stressful situations.
Tabatha Doherty was diagnosed at birth with complex congenital heart disease and had her first heart surgery at two weeks old; she has undergone seven surgeries.
John Bienvenu was diagnosed with stage four aggressive brain cancer at age 28, and his scans remained cancer free six years out, while only 5% of people with glioblastoma survive five or more years.
